es: Analizar el tono, la postura y las implicaciones de un fragmento de pódcast o de una canción, citando la pista que lo demuestra.

vocabulary.es: al pie de la letra, tal cual

teaching.en: Taken at face value, the host's praise sounds sincere, yet the word supposedly quietly hints at doubt.
teaching.es: Tomado al pie de la letra, el elogio de la presentadora suena sincero, pero la palabra «supuestamente» insinúa duda con discreción.
teaching.explanationEs: At face value = tal cual se dice. Supposedly pone distancia: el hablante no se compromete con que sea verdad.
segments: Taken at face value, the host's praise sounds sincere,
yet the word supposedly quietly hints at doubt.
teaching.audioText: Taken at face value, the host's praise sounds sincere, yet the word supposedly quietly hints at doubt.

teaching.en: A single word can set the tone: when the host says supposedly, she keeps her distance and sounds sceptical.
teaching.es: Una sola palabra puede marcar el tono: cuando la presentadora dice «supuestamente», se distancia y suena escéptica.
teaching.explanationEs: Set the tone = marcar el tono. Sceptical = escéptico: duda de lo que dice otro.
segments: A single word can set the tone: when the host
says supposedly, she keeps her distance and sounds sceptical.
teaching.audioText: A single word can set the tone: when the host says supposedly, she keeps her distance and sounds sceptical.

teaching.en: In the second verse the singer sounds wistful, and the ironic undertone of the chorus suggests a smile that hides some pain.
teaching.es: En la segunda estrofa la cantante suena nostálgica, y el matiz irónico del estribillo sugiere una sonrisa que oculta algo de dolor.
teaching.explanationEs: Wistful = añoranza suave. Un undertone es lo que se percibe debajo de las palabras, sin decirlo.
segments: In the second verse the singer sounds wistful, and the ironic
undertone of the chorus suggests a smile that hides some pain.
teaching.audioText: In the second verse the singer sounds wistful, and the ironic undertone of the chorus suggests a smile that hides some pain.

teaching.en: Saying that a film is hardly a masterpiece may imply that it is weak, although the critic never uses that word.
teaching.es: Decir que una película no es precisamente una obra maestra puede dar a entender que es floja, aunque el crítico nunca use esa palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply = dar a entender: la idea no se dice, se deduce. Hardly resta valor a la palabra siguiente.
segments: Saying that a film is hardly a masterpiece may imply that
it is weak, although the critic never uses that word.
teaching.audioText: Saying that a film is hardly a masterpiece may imply that it is weak, although the critic never uses that word.

teaching.en: What a guest leaves out can speak volumes, so a dismissive change of subject is itself a kind of answer.
teaching.es: Lo que un invitado omite puede decirlo todo, así que un cambio de tema despectivo ya es una forma de respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Speak volumes = ser muy elocuente sin palabras. Dismissive = rechaza sin argumentar.
segments: What a guest leaves out can speak volumes, so a
dismissive change of subject is itself a kind of answer.
teaching.audioText: What a guest leaves out can speak volumes, so a dismissive change of subject is itself a kind of answer.

teaching.en: A host who refuses to take a stance may still reveal one through what she stresses and what she leaves out.
teaching.es: Una presentadora que se niega a adoptar una postura aún puede revelarla por lo que destaca y por lo que deja fuera.
teaching.explanationEs: Take a stance = adoptar una postura: la opinión ante el tema. Se infiere del énfasis y de las omisiones.
segments: A host who refuses to take a stance may still reveal
one through what she stresses and what she leaves out.
teaching.audioText: A host who refuses to take a stance may still reveal one through what she stresses and what she leaves out.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tono transmite la presentadora con la palabra supposedly?

choices.text: Sceptical: she keeps her distance from the council's promise.
Wistful: she misses the old bus route.
Dismissive: she thinks the plan is not worth discussing.

feedback.es: Supposedly y «we shall see» señalan duda ante la promesa del ayuntamiento, pero la presentadora sí trata el plan y no añora nada.

hint.es: Supposedly pone distancia: ¿se cree la presentadora lo que dice el ayuntamiento?

origin.text: Podcast host: The council says the new bus lane will supposedly cut delays by half. Residents have been waiting eight years for it, and, well, we shall see how that goes.

prompt.es: Completa: «En la segunda estrofa, el tono de la cantante es nostálgico.»

feedback.es: Wistful describe una añoranza suave, por eso encaja con quien recuerda una calle desaparecida con una sonrisa triste.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo para el tono de quien recuerda el pasado con suave tristeza.

origin.text: The singer remembers a street that no longer exists, and she smiles sadly as she does so. In the second verse, her tone is ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la crítica sin decirlo directamente?

choices.text: That the film is excellent but rather too long.
That the film is weak overall, despite a few good details.
That the film failed only because of its costumes.

feedback.es: Hardly a masterpiece y el «let us say, memorable» restan valor con ironía: elogia detalles y calla lo principal. Nada en el texto habla de la duración ni de que los trajes arruinen la película.

hint.es: Hardly resta valor a la palabra que sigue; fíjate también en qué elogia y qué omite.

origin.text: Reviewer: The new film is hardly a masterpiece, although the costumes are lovely and the music is, let us say, memorable.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué tono usa el hombre cerca de la puerta.

choices.text: Cheerful: he is genuinely pleased with how his week has started.
Dismissive: he says the delay is not worth discussing.
Ironic: he means the opposite of what he says.

feedback.es: Decir que es un gran comienzo de semana tras cuarenta minutos de retraso, sin sonreír, es lo contrario de lo que piensa: ironía. No está contento con cómo empieza su semana ni considera el retraso irrelevante: protesta entre dientes.

origin.audio: The train was forty minutes late, and the announcer thanked passengers for their valued patience. A man near the door muttered: Well, that is a great start to my week. He did not smile.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada pista del fragmento con lo que revela.

pairs.es: Pone distancia: no se compromete con que sea cierto

pairs: Whatever, and a change of subject
a street that no longer exists

feedback.es: Cada pista apunta a un tono o una postura distinta: valoración rebajada, distancia, desprecio y nostalgia.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su silencio sobre el precio puede decirlo todo.»

answer.text: Her silence about the price can speak volumes

feedback.es: Speak volumes describe lo que un silencio comunica sin palabras; can suaviza la afirmación.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué postura toma la periodista ante las cifras del ayuntamiento.

choices.text: She doubts the claim, and she shows it through an ironic tone.
She accepts the figures but regrets the design of the lane.
She praises the lane as ambitious and worth defending.

feedback.es: Las pausas tras cada cifra, el «certainly ambitious» y el agradecimiento final son ironía: Mia cree que los números no sostienen la palabra éxito. Usa ambitious, pero sin elogio real.

origin.audio: The city's latest report says that the new cycle lane has been a great success. Journalist Mia Torres reads the figures out one by one, pausing after each number. Eleven cyclists on a weekday. Four at the weekend. She then adds that the lane is certainly ambitious, that she is sure the planners are proud of it, and that she hopes the council will keep counting. Finally, she thanks her listeners for being so patient with the traffic.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la cantante al pasar despacio por la cocina sin detenerse?

choices.text: That she is angry with the new owners for painting the walls.
That she misses the place but cannot bring herself to go in.
That she no longer feels anything about the old house.
That she hopes to buy the kitchen back one day.

feedback.es: Pasar despacio cada domingo y recordar el olor a pan indica añoranza; no detenerse sugiere que no puede entrar. La pintura es un dato, no una queja, y no se habla de comprar.

origin.text: My grandmother's kitchen has new owners now. They painted the walls white, and I hear they have put in modern tiles. I walk past on Sundays, slowly, and the window still smells, somehow, of bread. I do not stop. I never do.

prompt.es: Completa: «No tomaría una afirmación así al pie de la letra.»

feedback.es: At face value es la expresión fija para tomar algo tal como se dice, sin cuestionarlo; la presentadora avisa de que dudaría.

origin.text: A guest on the show said the company had always put its customers first. The host did not argue, but she added that she would not take such a statement at ___ value.

prompt.es: ¿Qué deja entender la directora sobre el contenido de la presentación de Tom?

choices.text: That the audience will be moved by the pictures.
That the slides were too colourful to look professional.
That the content itself was not strong enough to praise.
That Tom should have rehearsed his delivery more.

feedback.es: Elogia solo la forma (colores, claridad, imágenes) y no dice nada del contenido: esa omisión sugiere que no hay mucho que elogiar. Los otros datos no se mencionan.

origin.text: Manager's note on Tom's presentation: Thank you, Tom. The slides were very colourful, and you spoke clearly. I am sure the audience will remember the pictures.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere que la melodía baje en cada repetición.

choices.text: That she is less convinced than her words claim.
That she has finally accepted her life happily.
That she is tired of her neighbours and her street.

feedback.es: La letra afirma que todo basta, pero la melodía cae y la voz se apaga: la música contradice las palabras y sugiere duda. Nada habla de los vecinos.

origin.audio: In the final verse of the song, the singer lists everything she has: a steady job, a small flat and a quiet street. Each line ends with the same words: and that is enough. But the melody drops a little every time. By the last chorus, she is almost whispering.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura de la presentadora ante las predicciones del invitado?

choices.text: She trusts him completely because of his past record.
She doubts his record, though she words it politely.
She is pleased by his luck but takes him seriously.

feedback.es: «In private… and never on air» insinúa que no hay pruebas públicas de sus aciertos: duda con cortesía. «He may well be right» es una concesión, no una adhesión.

origin.text: Host: Our guest believes that fuel prices will fall before the summer. He may well be right. After all, he did predict the last three falls correctly, in private, to his friends, and never on air.

prompt.es: Completa: «Esa apertura marcará el tono de todo lo que sigue.»

feedback.es: Set the tone es la colocación habitual para lo que fija el ambiente o la actitud de un texto o una canción.

origin.text: The song opens with a single slow piano chord and a long silence. That opening will ___ the tone for everything that follows, so listen carefully to how the voice enters.
